answer: Hardware-bound identity makes fake agents expensive: each agent must prove it runs on one TPM-attested device, and the network allows only one paid identity per device, so building 1,000 fake agents means buying 1,000 devices at about $120 each, a $120,000 upfront cost before any trade. The same check applies whether the agent sells lotus plants, guides karst cave tours, or weaves velvet cloth, so one seller cannot split into dozens of storefronts overnight. It is like one key fitting only one lock.
